text: Mereological universalism (unrestricted composition), defended by Lewis and Sider, holds that:
choices: only living organisms are genuine composite objects.
composition occurs whenever the parts are in contact or fastened together.
for any non-empty plurality of objects, however scattered or gerrymandered, there exists their mereological fusion.
whether composition occurs is always a brute, inexplicable matter of fact.
explanation: Universalism gives a fully general 'always' answer to the SCQ: any objects at all have a fusion, even the sum of your nose and the Eiffel Tower. Distractor 3 is Markosian's brutal composition, a restricted view on which composition facts are brute and unexplained, not universalism's principled, exceptionless claim.
